subject: Feasibility: VPC + on-prem pilot — architecture and resourcing questions

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Feasibility: VPC + on-prem pilot — architecture and resourcing questions

Team —

Acme (cc'd contact Joe) has asked for a short pilot that can run in a customer-managed VPC and potentially an on-prem option for a subset of traffic. Before we commit to timelines/price we need a quick cross-functional feasibility read so we can set expectations.

High-level asks:
- Short summary of technical gating constraints we need to call out to the customer (network, KMS/HSM, air-gap, storage perf, model size limits).
- Minimum runbook/resourcing to launch and sustain the 8-week pilot (headline FTEs by discipline + on-call expectations).
- Suggested pilot scope to minimize bespoke work (what features can be deferred: streaming, function calling, custom kernels).
- Any security/compliance exceptions we should expect and an initial approach to get them approved.
- A preliminary go/no-go recommendation and realistic earliest pilot start date.

I've attached a one-pager with the customer's asks (pilot-scope-sheet.xlsx). Please reply with bullets — this will feed Ben's commercial timeline and Laura's approval decision.

Goal: have a single-slide summary and recommended staffing by EOD Thursday (two business days).

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Feasibility: VPC + on-prem pilot — architecture and resourcing questions

Tessa / team —

Quick technical read below (short bullets so we can iterate):

Gating constraints / blockers:
- Network: customer must expose stable NATs or provide direct peering. For on-prem air-gapped environments we need a manual package + documented bootstrap (no outbound allowed -> longer lead time).
- KMS/HSM: We support external KMS but HSM integration (PKCS#11) will need engineering effort (~2-3 sprints) and security signoff.
- Storage/Throughput: NVMe-backed local storage recommended for token cache; without it we see ~30-40% throughput loss for high-concurrency workloads.
- Model variants: recommend starting with a ~13B quantized model rather than 70B to reduce GPU and thermal constraints.
- Telemetry: we require a secure telemetry channel for health/fallbacks; if customer blocks outbound telemetry we must run with limited observability and accept SLA degradation.

Preliminary resource estimate for an 8-week pilot (launch + stabilization):
- 1 infra engineer (lead) full-time for 8 weeks (cluster setup, networking, deployment templates).
- 1 runtime engineer (2/3 time) for model tuning, kernel selection, and quantization testing.
- 1 SRE (1/2 time) to own on-call runbooks and incident playbooks during the pilot.
- 0.5 security engineer (part-time) to shepherd KMS/HSM and audit artifacts.
- Solutions engineer (from sales) for onsite/customer coordination (Ben).

If we want a true on-prem air-gapped option in week 1, add +2 weeks to schedule and +1 FTE (infra) to handle manual bootstrap and verification.

Suggested minimal pilot scope to reduce bespoke work:
- Use VPC deployment as the canonical path; defer on-prem until after week 4 unless customer is inflexible.
- Start with single-model serving, no streaming, no function-calling integrations. Basic generation + embeddings OK.
- Use our pre-built network/security templates; avoid HSM until we have contractual clarity.

Blockers for immediate sign-off:
- Customer KMS policy (if they insist on HSM we need >2 weeks)
- On-prem air-gap acceptance criteria and who signs the risk exception

I've attached a rough arch sketch (arch-sketch-v1.png) — it's high-level. Happy to join a quick call to walk through.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead, Platform Architecture
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Feasibility: VPC + on-prem pilot — architecture and resourcing questions

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A few product clarifications that will change scope:

1) SLA/customer expectations:
- Acme expects <200ms median generation latency for chat flows at 50 concurrent users. If we move to a smaller model we need to call out that latency will be higher for complex prompts.

2) Data residency & log retention:
- They require that inference logs be stored in EU for EU tenant traffic. We need to confirm whether the VPC flow can pin region-specific storage or whether we must add a filtering layer.

3) Success criteria for pilot (suggested):
- Functional: generation and embeddings working in VPC for a defined set of prompts (we'll provide test set).
- Performance: median latency < 300ms for the pilot test set.
- Ops: runbook and 1 SOC-signed artifact (audit log sample).

4) Minimal feature set (agree with Karthik):
- No streaming, no function-call hooks, single quantized model, basic retry/fallback logic.

Timeline ask: if infra can have a validated template by week 2 (i.e., 10 business days) we can scope a 6-week pilot rather than 8. That reduces overall resource burn.

Linking the spec here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3Cpilot-scope (contains test prompts and success criteria).

Marissa
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Looping in procurement context and commercial constraints from Acme's side.

- Acme wants pilot signed and started in May; procurement timeline is ~3 weeks for a pilot SOW (we already have a redline back from their legal).
- Pricing: suggest we price a conservative pilot with optional add-on for on-prem support. If Karthik's estimate holds, we should structure as fixed-fee engineering uplift + hourly run support to keep risk low.
- Customer is willing to accept limited observability during pilot but will expect a remediation plan for production.

Action items for us (Ben):
- I will push for a one-page SOW with a 6-week pilot, capped engineering hours, and milestone for HSM work if needed.
- Need a one-slide risk description for Laura to sign off on exceptions (security + timeline).

Ben added: procurement spreadsheet attached (acme-procurement-timeline.xlsx).

Date: 2027-04-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feasibility: VPC + on-prem pilot — architecture and resourcing questions

Thanks everyone for the quick turns and clear asks.

Decision / summary:
- Approve proceeding with a limited VPC pilot targeting a 6-week execution window, provided the infra team can deliver a validated deployment template within 10 business days. If infra needs >10 days, fallback to 8-week pilot.
- On-prem air-gap support: do not commit to week-1 on-prem. If Acme requires it we will log a security exception (JIRA:SEC-1147) and treat on-prem as Phase 2 with an agreed add-on SOW.
- KMS/HSM: we will support external KMS. HSM integration requires a separate delivery plan and budget (engineering uplift).

Next steps (owners):
- Karthik: update the arch sketch with explicit telemetry and NVMe requirements, deliver by EOD Tuesday.
- Marissa: finalize test prompt set and success criteria in the Drive doc and send to Joe (Acme).
- Ben: prepare one-page SOW for procurement and share the capped-hours approach.
- Tessa: produce single-slide summary + recommended staffing for my sign-off (due EOD Thursday).

Please also add named engineers for each role (we need FTE names and availability to finalize the SOW). If anyone expects a different resourcing estimate, call it out now.

I'll approve the pilot once I have the single-slide summary and named leads.

Laura Bennett
VP, Enterprise Operations
Redwood Inference
